## Strongest exact statement

The protected predecessor claim for candidate W89911 independently replays exactly under two separately implemented six-state two-symbol deterministic Turing-machine simulators on a bi-infinite blank tape. At both 250,000- and 1,000,000-transition budgets, W89911 halts after exactly 89,911 transitions, leaves exactly 185 ones, has visited-head span 541, and visits all six non-halting states A through F.

The complete 1-Hamming transition neighborhood also replays exactly. There are 12 transition entries and, for each entry, 27 alternative (write, move, next-state) triples, giving exactly 324 distinct single-transition mutants. Exhaustive replay to 250,000 transitions gives exactly 151 halting mutants and 173 mutants that do not halt within the budget; exactly zero halting mutants both visit all six non-halting states and exceed 89,911 transitions. The two independent implementations agree row-for-row on all 324 mutant outcomes, and canonical serialization of the full ledger has SHA-256 c745cff726fd0c89a11e31931f73190a0b4cdbba90e2052e0b3194321bd48cde.

## Derivation

The immutable WP08 task object was verified before substantive work: commit d92a09609b64a64e0faa26b04bc8432068e89e38 and task blob SHA-1 a03e746aa0025f8fdf927bfe140eb146e68d4f9e both match the registered identities exactly. The protected predecessor chain was then followed only far enough to recover the transition specification from its immutable protected packet; the immediately referenced WP07 source object also matched its recorded commit fb7d73f2e91ef13674853979835fe80725f6cf65 and blob SHA-1 cf5a823107f25f825ed9eb47f6dc07b451628a44, and the referenced WP06 packet matched blob SHA-1 4acb56dc846903d42f3104aee42ef1d7b8224a5e.

The replayed W89911 transition function is:
A0=(1,R,B), A1=(1,L,E);
B0=(1,R,C), B1=(1,R,B);
C0=(1,R,D), C1=(1,L,H);
D0=(1,L,A), D1=(1,L,D);
E0=(0,R,F), E1=(0,L,F);
F0=(1,L,C), F1=(0,L,A).

Implementation 1 used symbolic states A through F and H, with a sparse set containing exactly the tape cells holding one and explicit minimum/maximum visited head coordinates. Implementation 2 used integer states 0 through 6, a centered byte-array tape, incremental one-count maintenance, integer head deltas, and a six-bit reached-state mask. Their state representation, tape representation, and transition decoding are independent.

For the neighborhood audit, mutants were enumerated deterministically in state order A,B,C,D,E,F; current symbol 0,1; write 0,1; move L,R; next state A,B,C,D,E,F,H; with the original transition excluded. Each mutant was started on an all-zero tape with head at 0 and state A and executed for at most 250,000 transitions. Both engines produced identical complete result rows in the form [state,symbol,write,move,next,halted,steps,ones,span,sorted_reached_states]. Compact JSON serialization of the ordered 324-row array reproduced the predecessor fingerprint exactly.

## Assumptions beyond bootstrap

Only the protected packet's standard deterministic six-state two-symbol blank-tape semantics are assumed: a bi-infinite tape initially all zero, head initially at position 0, start state A, halting state H, and one transition counted for each applied transition including the transition entering H. Tape span is the inclusive interval between the minimum and maximum head positions visited after moves, matching the protected semantics. All counting, simulation, enumeration, and hashing are deterministic exact operations; no external Busy Beaver tables, hidden targets, empirical extrapolation, repository mutation, competition submission, or certification were used.
